extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors (especially at University of Utah) seeking which publishers allow zero-embargo repository deposit of article versions
extracted.subtask_description: A guide listing publishers and journals that permit authors to deposit some article version (typically the Author Accepted Manuscript) in non-profit repositories with no embargo, including timing, allowed versions, repository types, and special conditions. Useful for authors who must comply with funder zero-embargo/public-access requirements (e.g., NIH 2025 policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: General zero-embargo guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The following publishers or journals allow deposit of some version of the article, typically the Accepted Manuscript version, in a non-profit repository with no embargo even when the article is not available open access on the journal's website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to review these policies to confirm compatibility with federal funders' zero-embargo public access policies (e.g., NIH Public Access Policy effective July 1, 2025). To check a specific journal's policy on author article sharing (Green OA), use Open Policy Finder from Jisc. Contact Eccles Library for corrections or additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: AAAS / Science — Accepted Version posting immediately after publication
rubrics_metrics.description: "Authors of peer-reviewed research submitted to a Science subscription journal as of January 1, 2023, may post the Accepted Version of their paper on their personal or institutional archival website or in a repository of their choice immediately after publication."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed version: Accepted Version. Timing: immediately after publication. Repositories/sites: personal or institutional archival website or repository of choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: AACR — funder-required deposit timing and author responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors whose funders require deposition and release less than 6 months from the date of issue publication and who are not publishing in AACR's fully open access journal must make deposit arrangements themselves, with the appropriate release date no earlier than the date of issue publication in the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If funder requires release <6 months, authors must self-manage deposits and set release date to at least issue publication date; AACR's own fully OA journal is an exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIAA — permitted posting and repository limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of journal articles, magazine articles, and meeting papers published by AIAA may post their articles and papers on their private websites and deposit them in their institutional repositories, so long as access to the website is free of charge. Posting to an institutional repository is limited to those to which the author has a direct relationship (e.g., academic department repository, university repository, corporate intranet, agency repository, laboratory website, funding sources, or similar) including those that have deposit mandates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed versions: submitted (pre-print) or final accepted manuscript (revised after review). Repository restrictions: only repositories with a direct relationship to the author; must be free access. Applies to conference papers and journal articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIP — immediate deposit to institutional or funder-designated repositories
rubrics_metrics.description: "For institutional or funder-designated repositories (e.g., DOE Pages): You may deposit the accepted manuscript immediately after acceptance, using the credit line formatting below."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed version: accepted manuscript. Timing: immediately after acceptance. Use specified credit-line formatting; intended for institutional/funder-designated repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) — deposit in PMC or CDC Stacks immediately upon publication with permission
rubrics_metrics.description: "Authors may deposit the Author Accepted Manuscript (AAM) in PubMed Central or CDC Stacks immediately upon publication, with permission from the American Academy of Pediatrics."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing: immediately upon publication (note: wording implies deposit at publication rather than acceptance). Requires AAP permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: American College of Physicians (ACP) — deposit responsibility and allowed version
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is the responsibility of the author or grant recipient to comply with NIH requirements if their manuscript meets policy criteria. The version deposited should be the manuscript at acceptance, not the final published article."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must ensure NIH compliance where applicable. Allowed/deposited version: manuscript at acceptance (Author Accepted Manuscript), not the Version of Record.

rubrics_metrics.name: American Thoracic Society (ATS) — AAM distribution rights under CC BY 4.0 when required by funder
rubrics_metrics.description: Where required by their funder, authors retain the right to distribute their author accepted manuscript (AAM), such as via an institutional and/or subject repository (e.g. EuropePMC), under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license for release on or after the date of first online publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condition: applies when required by funder. Allowed license: CC BY 4.0. Timing: on or after first online publication. Repositories: institutional and/or subject repositories (example: EuropePMC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Association for Computing Machinery (ACM) — broad self-archiving/posting rights
rubrics_metrics.description: "All ACM published authors of magazine articles, journal articles, and conference papers retain the right to post the pre-submitted (also known as 'pre-prints'), submitted, accepted, and peer-reviewed versions of their work" on author homepage, institutional repository, or any repository legally mandated by funder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed versions: pre-prints, submitted, accepted, peer-reviewed (not necessarily final published version). Permitted sites: author's homepage, institutional repository, any legally mandated repository. This is explicit self-archiving/posting rights guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: BMJ — deposit AAM of NIH-funded research to NIHMS upon acceptance with zero embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: "BMJ will deposit the AAM of all NIH-funded research to NIHMS upon acceptance with zero embargo to comply with the latest NIH Public Access Policy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to NIH-funded research. Action: BMJ will deposit on behalf of authors to NIHMS at acceptance. Embargo: zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emerald — immediate/green OA deposit with publication visibility restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Emerald's green open access route allows authors to deposit their author accepted manuscript at any point, but it must not be made publicly accessible until official publication (i.e. as soon as it appears on Emerald Insight in its final typeset version).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may deposit AAM anytime, but public availability must wait until official publication; deposit can be in repository but not publicly accessible until Version of Record is live.

rubrics_metrics.name: European Mathematical Society (EMS) Press — AAM deposit allowed to institutional repositories and preprint servers
rubrics_metrics.description: For articles not published open access, EMS Press grants authors or their affiliated institutions the right to deposit the author accepted manuscript on institutional repositories and preprint servers. The accepted version is the article as accepted for publication, including all changes made during peer review, but not the version which is finally published and distributed by EMS Press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed version: Author Accepted Manuscript (post-review, pre-publisher final formatting). Repositories: institutional repositories and preprint servers. Applies only to non-open-access articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: IEEE — authors may follow funder public access mandates; default IEEE embargo 24 months
rubrics_metrics.description: IEEE policy provides that authors are free to follow funder public access mandates to post accepted articles in repositories. When posting in a repository, the IEEE embargo period is 24 months. However, IEEE recognizes that posting requirements and embargo periods vary by funder. IEEE authors may comply with requirements to deposit their accepted articles in a repository per funder requirements where the embargo is less than 24 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default IEEE embargo: 24 months for repository posting. Exception: authors may follow funder requirements if those require shorter embargo or immediate deposit; implies authors can comply with funders that require zero embargo even if IEEE default is longer.

rubrics_metrics.name: JAMA and JAMA Network — deposit AAM immediately on publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning in 2023, JAMA and all of the journals in the JAMA Network will adopt a new policy that permits authors of original research investigations to deposit their accepted manuscript in a public repository of their choosing immediately on the day that the manuscript is published by the JAMA Network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing: immediately on the day of publication. Allowed version: accepted manuscript. Scope: original research investigations in JAMA Network journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mary Ann Liebert — post accepted manuscript upon publication of Version of Record
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are welcome to post the accepted version of their manuscript to an institutional repository, funder repository, or personal website immediately upon publication of the Version of Record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing: immediately upon publication of Version of Record. Allowed repositories: institutional, funder, or personal website.

rubrics_metrics.name: PNAS — deposit accepted manuscript immediately upon publication to funder archive or noncommercial institutional repository
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediately upon publication, authors may deposit their accepted manuscript in their funding body’s archive or designated noncommercial institutional repository, under the same license as the published article, provided that a link to the published article in PNAS is included. Authors may make their deposited accepted manuscripts publicly available immediately upon publication by PNAS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing: immediately upon publication. Allowed license: same as published article. Requirement: must include link to the published article in PNAS. Repositories: funder archive or designated noncommercial institutional repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sage — share original submission or AAM any time after acceptance in any format
rubrics_metrics.description: You may share the Original Submission or Accepted Manuscript at any time after your paper is accepted and in any format. Your sharing may include posting a downloadable copy on any website, saving a copy in any repository or network, sharing via social media, and distributing print or electronic copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed versions: original submission and Accepted Manuscript. Timing: any time after acceptance. Formats/sites: any and all (websites, repositories, social media, print/electronic distribution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Wolters Kluwer / Lippincott — publisher deposit to PMC for OA; AAM deposit to PMC upon acceptance if not OA (from Jul 1, 2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: From Jul 01, 2025: if the article is published open access, the Journal will deposit the final published article to PubMed Central, on behalf of authors, for public availability without embargo on the official date of publication. If the article is not published open access, authors may comply with the policy by depositing their Author Accepted Manuscript to PubMed Central upon its acceptance for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two paths: (1) OA article: publisher deposits Version of Record to PMC at publication with zero embargo; (2) non-OA article: authors may deposit AAM to PMC upon acceptance to comply. Effective date: July 1, 2025.
